examples.label: Strings ending in abb
examples.purpose: Four states: any string of four or more symbols visits a state twice. Pumping the loop never changes the verdict.

examples.label: Even number of a's
examples.purpose: Two states, so the loop appears within two symbols. Pumping never changes the verdict.

examples.label: A loop of three symbols
examples.purpose: Accepts abc repeated, so y = abc: pumping repeats the whole cycle q0, q1, q2.

examples.label: Number literals
examples.purpose: Signed decimals with optional fraction and exponent (d is a digit). Eight states; the digit loops pump freely.

examples.label: aⁿbⁿ
examples.purpose: S repeats on the longest path: the a and b around the lower S are repeated or cut out together.

examples.label: Balanced parentheses
examples.purpose: A pair of parentheses around a balanced part can be repeated or removed.

examples.label: Expressions
examples.purpose: Several nonterminals repeat on the longest path; Another repeat cycles through them.

examples.label: A repeat two steps down
examples.purpose: S recurs through A, so v = ab and y = cd: the chain between the two S nodes is longer.

examples.label: Palindromes
examples.purpose: The repeated pair can sit anywhere: pumping the outer letters keeps the palindrome. Several repeats on the longest path.

examples.label: Mutual recursion
examples.purpose: A and B call each other: the repeated A is two steps below the first, so the path between them is drawn jagged.

examples.label: Nested data
examples.purpose: A JSON-like value: lists and records inside each other. Many repeats; pick another with the button.
text: M -> k : V , M | k : V | eps

examples.label: Nested expressions
examples.purpose: Right-recursive expressions with parentheses and unary minus: deep trees, repeats on several nonterminals.

examples.label: Long pieces
examples.purpose: v and y are three symbols long: the columns of the figure are wide.
text: S -> a b c S d e f | x

examples.label: if–then–else
examples.purpose: Terminals of several characters, separated by spaces in the input; an ambiguous grammar, of which the parser finds one tree.
text: S -> if E then S else S | if E then S | a
strings: if e then if e then a else a

examples.label: Regular expressions
examples.purpose: A larger grammar: the repeated nonterminal is several steps below the first one on the longest path.
